findings.title: Do not execute an unpinned remote script as root
findings.whyItBreaks: Docker builds run this command as root, so whoever controls or changes the HTTPS endpoint can execute arbitrary commands and change the image contents. There is no version pin, checksum, signature, or vendored source.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: In Alpine's `/bin/sh`, pipeline status comes from the final `sh` process. A failed `curl` can therefore be masked by `sh` exiting successfully on empty input, producing an image that appears successfully built without running the installer.

findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: `https://example.com/install.sh` currently returns 404, and `curl -sL ... | sh` feeds that HTML to the shell, causing the image build to fail. If the endpoint later serves content, the unpinned remote script executes with build privileges and can poison the image or access build-time data.

findings.title: Stop piping an unpinned remote script into the root shell
findings.whyItBreaks: Every image build grants arbitrary current content served by https://example.com/install.sh root-level code execution, with no pinned artifact, checksum, or signature. A compromised server, redirect target, or intermediary can alter the image build.

findings.title: Make installer download failures fail the image build
findings.whyItBreaks: The curl status is discarded by the pipe. On a transport failure, curl can produce no input while sh exits successfully, so Docker reports a successful build containing none of the installer changes.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in the exported loader
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing when the key is absent, but this exported helper ignores that error and returns "". A missing key is therefore indistinguishable from a present key whose value is legitimately empty, forcing callers to act on a failure as if it were data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in the public loader
findings.whyItBreaks: LoadOrDefault ignores ErrMissing, so callers cannot distinguish a missing key from a key whose legitimate value is "". Because this is an exported API with no explicit fallback or presence indicator, every caller is forced to conflate failure with data.

findings.title: Do not discard ErrMissing in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for absent keys at src/store.go:10, but this exported helper ignores that error and returns "". Callers cannot distinguish a missing key from a present key containing an empty string.

findings.title: Wait for spawned result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation guaranteed that every result send completed before Run returned. The new goroutines let Run return immediately; a caller that closes results after Run returns can race with these sends and panic, and callers treating return as completion can observe missing results.

findings.title: Wait for worker sends before returning from Run
findings.whyItBreaks: Each result send runs in a detached goroutine, so Run can return while outputs are still pending or blocked. Callers that use Run's return as completion can observe missing results, and callers that close the channel afterward can trigger a send-on-closed-channel panic.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning from Run
findings.whyItBreaks: Each result send now runs asynchronously, so Run can return while jobs remain undelivered. Callers that consume results after Run returns can observe an incomplete batch, and callers that close results after Run returns can trigger a concurrent send-on-closed-channel panic.

findings.title: Keep Log's original function type for source compatibility
findings.whyItBreaks: Log changed from func(string) to func(string, ...string). Existing consumers assigning logger.Log to a func(string) variable, passing it to a func(string) parameter, or storing it behind that type no longer compile, even though direct one-argument calls still work.

findings.title: Require admin status and tenant match before deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing && to || authorizes any non-admin in the record's tenant and allows an admin to delete records from another tenant, bypassing both the admin gate and tenant isolation enforced by the previous implementation.

findings.title: Restore tenant matching in deletion authorization
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing && to || makes any administrator authorized to delete a record from another tenant, bypassing tenant isolation enforced by the previous condition.

findings.title: Preserve tenant isolation for admin deletions
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing && to || makes canDeleteRecord return true for any admin session, even when the record belongs to another tenant. An admin from tenant A can therefore delete tenant B's records; the previous implementation required both admin status and matching tenant.

findings.title: Preserve parse errors instead of returning defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, JSON and validation errors reached updateFontSize and prevented saving. Now invalid input returns DEFAULTS; updateFontSize then saves those defaults with the requested font size, so input such as {"theme":"dark","fontSize":"bad"} silently loses the user's dark theme.

findings.title: Do not swallow settings parse failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, JSON and validation errors propagated from parseSettings, so updateFontSize did not save. Now parseSettings returns DEFAULTS; for raw '{"theme":"dark"}', updateFontSize receives theme 'light' and saves it with the new font size, silently losing the user's theme.

findings.title: Do not persist defaults after a settings parse failure
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch converts malformed JSON or invalid fields into DEFAULTS. updateFontSize then accepts that fallback and saves it, so invalid/corrupt input now silently overwrites the stored theme instead of propagating the parse error and performing no write.

findings.title: Use the requested commit when loading report artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: For any branch whose ref differs from the fixed `verified` ref, the report claims `builtFrom` is the branch commit but lists artifacts from another commit. This produces an internally inconsistent and incorrect build report.

findings.title: Use the requested branch commit when loading artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: The report still declares builtFrom as the requested branch's commit, but now loads artifacts from the hardcoded `verified` ref. When those refs differ, the report silently associates the wrong artifacts with the reported commit.

findings.title: Collect artifacts from the requested commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The report still identifies builtFrom as build.ref(branch), but artifacts are now read from build.ref("verified"). Whenever those refs differ, the returned report combines metadata from two commits and displays artifacts that were not produced by the reported build.

findings.title: Preserve the limit when returning sorted entries
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit, recentEntries now returns every reversed entry instead of at most limit entries. renderFeed passes 20 at src/feed.ts:9, so inputs with more than 20 entries produce an output longer than the intended 20-entry page.

findings.title: Preserve the limit when returning sorted entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The function's contract promises at most `limit` entries, but `return sorted` returns every input entry. renderFeed calls it with 20 and then writes every returned entry, expanding its nominal 20-entry output when `all.length` exceeds 20.

findings.title: Keep recentEntries capped for positive limits
findings.whyItBreaks: The function's public contract promises at most `limit` entries, but the new return path returns the entire reversed array for every positive limit. `renderFeed` calls it with 20 at line 9; when `all.length` exceeds 20, assignments beyond the initial 20-element array expand `out`, so the caller receives the entire feed instead of one page.

findings.title: Count only emitted live rows in entry-count
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, the manifest declares entries.length but emits only live rows. For example, one stale and one live entry produces entry-count: 2 with one data row, so consumers that trust the header can misparse or reject the manifest.

findings.title: Keep entry-count synchronized with filtered rows
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, the rendered manifest contains fewer data rows than the `# entry-count` header reports because the header still uses `entries.length` at line 22. Consumers that trust the count can reject, truncate, or misparse the manifest.

findings.title: Count only the entries emitted into the manifest
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, it is removed from rows but line 22 still emits entries.length. For two inputs with one stale entry, the manifest declares entry-count: 2 while containing only one data row, so consumers relying on the header misparse or reject the manifest.

findings.title: Preserve the exported FormatLegacyID API
findings.whyItBreaks: FormatLegacyID is an exported function in a non-internal package. Any downstream code calling ids.FormatLegacyID will no longer compile after these deletions, regardless of the absence of in-repo callers.

score.error: critic produced no summary or checked list (likely malformed output)

findings.title: Preserve the exported FormatLegacyID API
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing this exported function causes any downstream package that calls ids.FormatLegacyID to fail compilation with an undefined symbol on upgrade.

findings.title: Preserve the exported shippingQuote API
findings.whyItBreaks: shippingQuote was an exported function from src/orders.ts, but this change removes it without a compatibility export. Existing consumers importing shippingQuote now fail to compile or resolve the symbol, even though the implementation was only moved.

findings.title: Preserve the exported shippingQuote API
findings.whyItBreaks: The base module exported shippingQuote, but this change removes that export and only exposes quoteShipping from a different module. Existing consumers importing shippingQuote from src/orders will fail to compile after the upgrade.

findings.title: Preserve the shippingQuote export from orders.ts
findings.whyItBreaks: shippingQuote was previously exported by src/orders.ts, but the new module only exports quoteShipping and orders.ts no longer re-exports the old symbol. Existing imports from src/orders fail to compile or resolve at runtime.

findings.title: Restore execute's successful uppercase return
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call to execute now throws Error("always fails") instead of returning the uppercase string implemented on the base branch, making the exported function unusable.

findings.title: Preserve execute's successful return behavior
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed implementation unconditionally throws, so callers of the exported function cannot receive the uppercase string previously returned for any input.

findings.title: Restore execute's successful return path
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call to the exported execute function now throws Error("always fails") instead of returning the uppercase string previously produced, making the API unusable.

findings.title: Do not reject viewers before read-only handling
findings.whyItBreaks: The new eligibility gate rejects every viewer, making handle's existing viewer branch at line 25 unreachable. An active viewer with fewer than five attempts changed from "read-only" to "rejected".

findings.title: Keep active viewers on the read-only path
findings.whyItBreaks: For an active viewer with fewer than five attempts, isEligible now returns false, so handle returns "rejected" at line 24 before reaching its existing "read-only" branch at line 25. This regresses the previously supported viewer behavior.

findings.title: Preserve read-only handling for active viewers
findings.whyItBreaks: The new viewer rejection causes handle() at src/handler.ts:24 to return "rejected" before its existing viewer-specific "read-only" branch at line 25. Every active viewer with fewer than five attempts therefore changes from read-only access to rejection.

findings.title: Do not require payment to save a draft
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed now returns false for {state:"draft", payment:"missing"}. saveDraft relies on this predicate, so users can no longer save an unpaid draft even though saving a draft does not require payment.

findings.title: Do not require payment when saving a draft
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed now requires payment === "paid". saveDraft calls this predicate, so a legitimate draft order with payment "missing" is returned as "blocked" instead of being saved. Payment approval should govern submission, not draft persistence.

findings.title: Do not require payment when saving a draft
findings.whyItBreaks: For an order with state="draft" and payment="missing", canProceed now returns false. saveDraft calls this predicate at src/actions.ts:9, so a valid unpaid draft returns "blocked" instead of "saved". Payment is relevant to submitting an order, not persisting an unfinished draft.

findings.title: Read files from the published channel commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The snapshot's commit is resolved from the requested channel, but its files are read from stable. Whenever those refs differ, the snapshot claims one commit while publishing another channel's contents.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the requested commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned snapshot declares commit=headCommit(channel) but loads filesAt(stable). Whenever the requested channel differs from stable, consumers receive file contents that do not belong to the advertised commit.

findings.title: Read files from the published channel's commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The snapshot reports commit=headCommit(channel) but loads filesAt(headCommit("stable")). For any channel whose head differs from stable, consumers receive stable's contents labeled as the channel commit.

findings.title: Apply the new limit parameter when building output
findings.whyItBreaks: The public build(prefix, limit=10) signature promises a caller-controlled cap, but the implementation always sets max_count to 10. Calling build('x', 3) still returns 10 items.

findings.title: Honor the new limit parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: The public signature promises that limit controls the number of generated items, but the body hardcodes max_count = 10. For example, build('x', 3) still returns 10 items.

findings.title: Honor the new limit parameter when building output
findings.whyItBreaks: build now accepts limit, but the body still hard-codes max_count = 10, so build("x", limit=3) returns 10 items instead of 3.

findings.title: Reject non-positive values in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but its body simply returns int(value). Thus parse_positive_int(-1) and parse_positive_int(0) succeed, and charge() produces negative or zero cents instead of rejecting invalid input.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but simply returns int(value). charge(-1) therefore returns -100 instead of rejecting invalid input.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but its implementation only calls int(value). charge relies on that promise, so parse_positive_int('-3') returns -3 and charge produces -300 cents instead of rejecting the invalid amount.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation copied df before applying mappings, while this version writes directly into the caller-owned DataFrame. Any caller retaining the original object now observes modified values, changing the function's established behavior and potentially corrupting later processing.

findings.title: Keep apply_values from mutating its input DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation copied df before applying mappings. The changed assignment writes directly into the caller's DataFrame, so callers that reuse the original now observe unexpected value updates and may lose the pre-transform state.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation copied df before applying mappings, while this line now writes directly to the caller-owned DataFrame. Callers that retain or reuse the original input will observe unexpected value changes and can no longer treat the returned result as an independent transformed copy.

findings.title: Enforce the positivity promised by parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The public function name promises a positive integer, but the body returns any parsed i64, including negatives, and maps invalid input to 0. The in-repo caller then multiplies that value, so charge("-1") produces -100 instead of rejecting invalid input.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: parse_positive_int("-2") returns -2 because the body only parses and defaults errors to zero. charge("-2") therefore produces -200, allowing a negative charge despite the function's public contract.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The public function name promises a positive integer, but the body accepts negatives and zero. charge() relies on it, so charge("-1") returns -100 instead of rejecting or producing a non-negative amount.

findings.title: Borrow items before debugging it
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg!(items) consumes the Vec<String>; the next line accesses items.len(), producing a Rust use-after-move compile error.

findings.title: Borrow items instead of moving them into dbg!
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg!(items) consumes the Vec<String>; the subsequent items.len() use at line 3 triggers Rust's moved-value error, breaking compilation.

findings.title: Borrow items instead of moving them into dbg!
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg!(items) consumes the Vec<String> expression; the subsequent items.len() at line 3 uses the moved value, producing a Rust E0382 compile error.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the pinned revision
findings.whyItBreaks: When `latest` differs from `pinnedTag`, `changedPaths` is computed relative to `latest` but `fromRevision` still reports the pinned revision. Consumers replay these paths on the pinned revision, producing an incomplete or incorrect changeset.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the advertised base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned fromRevision is the pinned revision, but changedPaths are computed from latest. Consumers replaying the changeset on fromRevision can receive an incorrect path set.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the pinned revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The changeset declares `fromRevision` as the resolved pinned tag, but `changedPaths` is now computed relative to `latest`. Consumers replay these paths on `fromRevision`, so the path set can omit, include, or otherwise mismatch the changes between the declared base and target.

findings.title: Update queries to use the renamed contact_email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration renames users.email to users.contact_email, src/query.sql still executes SELECT email FROM users, which fails because email no longer exists.

findings.title: Update queries after renaming the users column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, `users.email` no longer exists, but `src/query.sql:1` still executes `SELECT email FROM users`, causing the read to fail with an unknown-column error.

findings.title: Update users.email consumers with the column rename
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, users.email no longer exists, but src/query.sql still executes SELECT email FROM users, which fails with a missing-column error.

findings.title: Stop embedding a live billing API key in source
findings.whyItBreaks: makeClient() ignores BILLING_API_KEY and always returns the committed bk_live_ credential. Deployments authenticate with the wrong shared credential, missing configuration no longer fails closed, and the credential is exposed to anyone with repository access.

findings.title: Restore environment-sourced billing credentials
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported client now returns the same `bk_live_` credential in every deployment. Anyone with repository access can use it, environments cannot isolate or rotate credentials, and missing configuration no longer fails closed.

findings.title: Do not hardcode the live billing API key
findings.whyItBreaks: The source now embeds a bk_live credential, so anyone with repository access can use it. All deployments also ignore BILLING_API_KEY and cannot rotate credentials through configuration.

findings.title: Preserve the admin requirement for project purges
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed guard returns forbidden when user.isAdmin is true, so any non-admin with an archived project reaches db.delete and receives "purged". The previous implementation allowed only admins to delete archived projects.

findings.title: Restore admin-only authorization before deleting projects
findings.whyItBreaks: With user.isAdmin=false and project.archived=true, both guards pass and db.delete(project.id) executes, so a non-admin can purge an archived project. With user.isAdmin=true and project.archived=true, line 12 returns forbidden and blocks the previously authorized purge.

findings.title: Restore admin-only authorization for archived purges
findings.whyItBreaks: For a non-admin archived project, line 12 is skipped and line 13 is also skipped, so db.delete runs at line 14. Admins are instead immediately rejected. This reverses the previous authorization behavior and permits unauthorized destructive deletion.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-config fallback in startup
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings() explicitly returns None when the path does not exist, but startup now indexes settings unconditionally. A missing configuration therefore raises TypeError instead of returning the prior default worker count of 1.

findings.title: Handle missing settings before subscripting
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None for a nonexistent path, and this line now evaluates settings["workers"] directly, raising a TypeError. The previous fallback allowed startup to continue with one worker.

findings.title: Preserve defaults when the settings file is missing
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None for a nonexistent path, and startup now immediately evaluates settings["workers"], raising TypeError. Before this change it returned the default worker count of 1.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures from Charge
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, a Submit error reached the caller as a non-nil wrapped error at pay/charge.go:14. The new path only logs it and returns nil at line 17, forcing callers of this exported API to treat failed charges as successful.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures from Charge
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge only logs it and returns nil. Callers of this exported API cannot distinguish a failed charge from a successful one and may proceed as though payment completed.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures from Charge
findings.whyItBreaks: When gw.Submit returns an error, Charge now logs it and returns nil. Callers cannot distinguish a failed payment from a successful charge and may record or act on a payment that was never completed.

findings.title: Keep settings cache keys scoped to tenant
findings.whyItBreaks: The process-wide cache now keys only by setting name. After tenant A fetches a setting, tenant B requesting the same name gets A's cached value without calling its own store, causing cross-tenant data disclosure and incorrect configuration. The changed invalidate signature also cannot target a tenant-specific entry.

findings.title: Keep tenant identity in settings cache keys
findings.whyItBreaks: cacheKey ignores tenantId, so after tenant A fetches a setting, tenant B requesting the same name hits A's cached value and never calls store.fetch for B.

findings.title: Keep tenant IDs in settings cache keys
findings.whyItBreaks: cacheKey ignores tenantId, so after one tenant caches a setting, another tenant requesting the same name gets the first tenant's value from the cache and skips its own store.fetch call.

findings.title: Serialize concurrent reservations before persisting stock
findings.whyItBreaks: Two concurrent reserve calls can both read the same positive remaining count before either await completes, both save remaining - 1, and both return true. With one item in stock, this allows two successful reservations.

findings.title: Preserve compatibility for zero-argument Inventory construction
findings.whyItBreaks: Inventory was constructible without arguments; this required parameter makes existing TypeScript consumers fail to compile, while JavaScript consumers get an undefined store and a runtime TypeError on reserve.

findings.title: Do not silently change reserve from boolean to Promise
findings.whyItBreaks: reserve previously returned a boolean. Existing JavaScript callers checking its truthiness will now treat the Promise as success even when the eventual result is false, and typed callers expecting boolean no longer compile.

findings.title: Serialize concurrent reservations per SKU
findings.whyItBreaks: Two concurrent reserve calls read the same remaining count before either awaited save. Both persist and then set remaining - 1, so two calls can return true while only one unit is consumed.

findings.title: Serialize concurrent reservations before persisting
findings.whyItBreaks: Two concurrent reserve calls can both read the same positive remaining count, both await save, and both return true while decrementing stock only once. With stock=1, Promise.all of two calls can report two successful reservations.

findings.title: Stop multiplying the millisecond backoff in retry
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff(0) now returns 1000 milliseconds, but src/jobs/retry.ts:12 still multiplies it by 1000, making the first retry wait 1,000,000 ms instead of 1,000 ms; later retries are similarly delayed from seconds to minutes or hours.

findings.title: Remove the stale seconds-to-milliseconds conversion in retry
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff() now returns milliseconds, but retry() still multiplies that value by 1000 at src/jobs/retry.ts:12. The first retry waits 1,000,000 ms (about 16m40s) instead of 1,000 ms, and the capped delay becomes about 8h20m instead of 30s.

findings.title: Stop multiplying the millisecond backoff in retry
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff() now returns milliseconds: attempt 0 is 1000 and the cap is 30000. retry() still calls sleep(backoff(a) * 1000), so the first retry waits 1000000 ms (~16.7 minutes) instead of 1000 ms, and the cap becomes 30000000 ms (~8.3 hours).

findings.title: Propagate close errors from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred f.Close() error is ignored. Previously, Save returned f.Close()'s error after a successful flush; now a close-time write or persistence failure is indistinguishable from success.

findings.title: Preserve close errors from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred f.Close() ignores its error. Previously, Save returned the close error after flushing; close-time write or filesystem failures can now return nil and be indistinguishable from a successful save.

findings.title: Propagate file-close errors from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The new deferred Close ignores its return value. If the filesystem reports a delayed write or close failure after Flush succeeds, Save returns nil and callers cannot distinguish failed persistence from success. The previous implementation returned f.Close() and propagated that error.

findings.title: Iterate through the full half-open page window
findings.whyItBreaks: _window_bounds returns half-open [start, end) bounds, but range(start, end - 1) excludes the last valid position. Every rendered page loses its final row; page_size=1 produces empty pages.

findings.title: Preserve public keyword parameter names
findings.whyItBreaks: Renaming public parameters changes keyword-call compatibility. Existing calls such as page_count(total=3, size=2) now raise TypeError; the same break applies to the renamed parameters of clamp, page_window, render_page, and summarize.

findings.title: Include the final row in each page window
findings.whyItBreaks: The documented half-open bounds are [start, end), but range(start, end - 1) excludes the valid index end - 1. Every non-empty page loses its last row, and page_size=1 produces empty pages.

findings.title: Iterate through the page's end bound
findings.whyItBreaks: The documented bounds are half-open [start, end), but range(start, end - 1) excludes end - 1. Every page loses its last row, and pages of size 1 render empty.

findings.title: Restore the TTL freshness check
findings.whyItBreaks: Fresh entries with elapsed time below ttlMs are deleted and reported as misses, while expired entries with elapsed time above ttlMs are returned indefinitely as stale values.

findings.title: Remove completed jobs without skipping adjacent entries
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing during forward forEach shifts the next job into the current index, then iteration advances past it. For example, two adjacent done jobs leave the second job in the returned array.

findings.title: Return cache entries only while they are within the TTL
findings.whyItBreaks: The comparison is reversed: fresh entries with age below the TTL are deleted and reported as misses, while expired entries with age above the TTL are returned as valid values.

findings.title: Avoid splicing completed jobs during forward iteration
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing an item shifts the next job left while forEach advances its index, so adjacent completed jobs are skipped. For example, two consecutive done jobs leave the second one in the returned queue.

findings.title: Restore the TTL freshness comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: The age check now returns values only when age is greater than ttlMs, so fresh entries are deleted and expired entries are served as valid.

findings.title: Use non-mutating filtering to prune every completed job
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing during indexed forEach shifts later jobs left; with adjacent done jobs, one is skipped and remains. It also mutates the caller's array, unlike the previous implementation.

findings.title: Preserve numeric ordering when ranking scores
findings.whyItBreaks: scores.sort() compares numbers lexicographically, then reverse() produces reverse lexicographic order rather than descending numeric order. For scores 2 and 10 with n=1, the cutoff becomes 2 and topPlayers can return the 2-point player instead of the 10-point player; formatBoard exposes the wrong leaderboard.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before computing the cutoff
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() without a comparator orders numbers as strings. For scores [2, 10], reverse() yields [2, 10], so topPlayers(..., 1) computes a cutoff of 2 and returns the player with score 2 instead of the player with score 10.

findings.title: Preserve numeric ordering when ranking scores
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() compares numbers as strings. For players with scores [3, 20, 100] and n=1, rankScores returns [3, 20, 100], cutoff becomes 3, and the unchanged filter/slice returns the first input player (score 3) instead of the highest scorer.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality may return after the first mismatching character, leaking attacker-controlled signature prefix information. With repeated timing measurements, this can weaken HMAC verification and potentially enable forged webhook requests to reach processor(payload) through handle at line 14.

findings.title: Preserve constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Python string equality can return after the first mismatching character, so remote attackers can use verification timing to incrementally recover the valid HMAC signature and potentially forge webhook requests.

findings.title: Keep constant-time comparison for webhook signatures
findings.whyItBreaks: 普通 string equality exits based on the first mismatching character, exposing the expected HMAC through response timing and making forged webhook signatures feasible with repeated requests. The previous hmac.compare_digest call avoided this side channel.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction commits after recording the ledger at line 23, before _apply_balances runs. If either balance update fails, the ledger remains committed and the source account may already be debited without the destination being credited.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction commits after recording the ledger, before _apply_balances runs. If either balance update fails, the ledger entry remains committed while balances are unchanged or only partially updated, so the transfer is no longer atomic.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction commits after _record_ledger returns, before _apply_balances runs. If either balance update fails, the ledger entry remains committed while balances are unchanged or only partially updated.

findings.title: Preserve UTC semantics for billing-day calculation
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing UTC getters with local getters makes the same instant produce different billing days on hosts in different timezones. For example, 2024-01-01T00:30:00Z becomes 2023-12-31 in America/Los_Angeles, whereas the previous implementation returned 2024-01-01.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving billing days
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing the UTC getters with local-time getters changes the billing date for instants near midnight whenever the process timezone is non-UTC. For example, 23:30 UTC can be assigned to the prior local calendar day, and sameBillingDay inherits that misclassification.

findings.title: Preserve UTC semantics for billing-day calculation
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation used UTC getters, but this now uses local getters. For example, 2024-01-01T23:30:00Z becomes 2024-01-02 in a UTC+8 process instead of 2024-01-01; sameBillingDay inherits the misclassification.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: Using only account as the key makes readProfile("tenant-a", "same-account") cache tenant A's profile, after which readProfile("tenant-b", "same-account") returns that cached profile without calling tenant B's fetcher. This leaks profile data across tenants and returns the wrong tenant's display name.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A loads account X, tenant B requesting the same account X receives tenant A's cached profile without calling fetchProfile. This exposes incorrect cross-tenant profile data and prevents tenant B's profile from being loaded.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: Profiles are fetched with both tenant and account, but the shared memo now keys only by account. If two tenants use the same account identifier, the second request receives the first tenant's cached Profile without calling fetchProfile, causing cross-tenant data exposure and incorrect profile data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch intercepts the Error thrown for a missing key at line 4 and returns "" instead. loadAll therefore converts missing entries into ordinary empty values, so callers cannot distinguish absent data from a valid empty string.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors instead of returning an empty string
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, a missing key raised the error at src/store.ts:4. The new catch converts that failure to "", which is indistinguishable from a legitimately stored empty string; loadAll consequently returns successful-looking arrays containing missing values, and public callers cannot detect the failure.

findings.title: Preserve load failures instead of returning an empty string
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous missing-key error at src/store.ts:3 propagated to callers. The new catch returns "", which is also a valid value in Map<string, string>; callers can no longer distinguish a missing key or other failure from stored empty data. Because load is exported, this is a broken public contract even without in-repository callers.

findings.title: Propagate the final failure from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: Every exception from fn is caught and discarded, and exhausting retries returns normally with void. Callers cannot distinguish a successful background operation from one that failed on every attempt, so failure can be treated as success.

findings.title: Preserve timeoutMs compatibility for existing retry callers
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing callers supplying timeoutMs now have config.timeout undefined; Date.now() + undefined becomes NaN, so the deadline guard at line 10 never expires and the configured timeout is silently bypassed. Existing TypeScript callers also fail because retries and timeout are now required.

findings.title: Expose callback failure from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: The new exported function catches every callback exception and returns normally after retries are exhausted, so callers cannot distinguish successful execution from total failure and may treat failed background work as successful.

findings.title: Preserve the existing retry configuration contract
findings.whyItBreaks: Config is exported and is consumed by retry. Existing callers providing {maxAttempts, timeoutMs} no longer type-check because retries is newly required and timeoutMs was removed. Unmigrated JavaScript callers get config.timeout === undefined, producing a NaN deadline so the timeout guard never fires.

findings.title: Propagate exhaustion errors from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported retryBackground catches every exception and, after retries are exhausted or the deadline expires, returns void. Public callers cannot distinguish a successful callback from a failed callback, so failure can be treated as success.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now publicly accepts number, but value.length is invalid for the number branch. TypeScript rejects this union access; if transpiled without typechecking, numeric values render as "len=undefined".

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading their length
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now publicly accepts number values, but value.length is invalid for the string | number union. TypeScript reports that length does not exist on number; if transpiled without type-checking, numeric inputs produce len=undefined.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading their length
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now publicly accepts number at line 2, but value.length is invalid for the number branch. TypeScript rejects this union access; if type checking is bypassed, numeric values produce defaultValue="len=undefined".

findings.title: Do not echo the deployment token into workflow logs
findings.whyItBreaks: Every push exposes TOKEN to the shell and prints its value to the workflow log. Log masking is best-effort and does not make secret output safe; a token value that is not masked is disclosed to anyone with log access.

findings.title: Do not print the deployment token in workflow logs
findings.whyItBreaks: The step expands TOKEN and writes its full value to stdout. This exposes a deployment credential to the workflow log pipeline and any downstream log collection; secret masking is not a safe substitute for never logging credentials.

findings.title: Preserve the large-output buffer for git review commands
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores Node's 1 MiB spawnSync default. The git diff used to build the review patch at line 140 can exceed that for a large PR, causing spawnSync to fail and runGithub to report a failed review instead of reviewing the change.

findings.title: Restore the 64 MiB buffer for git diff output
findings.whyItBreaks: spawnSync now uses Node's approximately 1 MiB default maxBuffer. The git diff at line 140 can exceed that for a large PR, causing spawnSync to fail and runGithub to post a failed review/check instead of reviewing the change.

findings.title: Preserve the large git output buffer
findings.whyItBreaks: spawnSync now uses Node's 1 MiB default maxBuffer instead of the previous 64 MiB limit. The git diff at line 140 can exceed that for a large PR, causing truncated output/process failure and making runGithub post a failed review check instead of reviewing the PR.

findings.title: Restore the explicit read-only sandbox for review runs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` makes Codex inherit its user/configured sandbox policy. In writable configurations, model-generated commands can modify or delete files under `opts.repoPath`, so the review wrapper no longer guarantees non-mutating execution.

findings.title: Preserve the read-only sandbox for review subprocesses
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` makes `codex exec` inherit user/project sandbox settings. With a workspace-write or danger-full-access configuration, untrusted repository content can prompt the review agent to modify or delete files, execute commands, or affect data outside the intended read-only review.

findings.title: Keep Codex execution pinned to the read-only sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: Without `-s read-only`, `codex exec` can inherit a workspace-write or danger-full-access policy from Codex configuration. A prompt or repository instruction can then modify `opts.repoPath` during review, potentially hiding changes or causing the reviewer to return a verdict for a tampered tree.

findings.title: Compute the review range from the merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_BASE_SHA is the base-branch tip, which may include commits made after the PR branched. Diffing baseSha..HEAD therefore includes unrelated base changes and can omit PR changes when both tips contain the same final file state. The same incorrect range drives changedFiles, so review classification and inline comments can target the wrong files.

findings.title: Build the review from the supplied PR head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_HEAD_SHA is supplied but the checkout's HEAD is a merge commit or stale revision, patch and changedPaths are computed from HEAD while postReview/postCheck target headSha at line 178. The review can therefore analyze a different tree than the commit receiving the review, causing incorrect or rejected inline comments.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base rather than the base branch tip
findings.whyItBreaks: For a PR whose base branch advanced after the topic branch forked, git diff baseSha HEAD is a two-tree comparison that includes base-only changes. The review bundle and changedPaths therefore contain unrelated files, producing false findings or inline comments on changes not made by the PR.

findings.title: Use PR_HEAD_SHA when constructing the review diff
findings.whyItBreaks: headSha honors PR_HEAD_SHA, but the patch and changed-file set now hardcode HEAD. When the environment points to a PR commit while cwd is a merge commit or stale checkout, the bundle reviews the wrong code and inline comments are based on the wrong file set, potentially approving or annotating an unrelated revision.

findings.title: Preserve literal prompt data during placeholder substitution
findings.whyItBreaks: String.replace interprets $&, $`, $', and $$ in a replacement string. A patch or bundle value containing one of these sequences is rewritten instead of inserted literally; for example, a patch containing "$&" inserts the diff --git a/src/core/review.ts b/src/core/review.ts placeholder into the critic prompt. The same regression exists in the FINDINGS and PATCH substitutions on lines 32-33, causing the model to review corrupted or incomplete input.

findings.title: Preserve literal patch text during prompt interpolation
findings.whyItBreaks: String replacement values interpret `$&`, `$``, and `$'` specially. A valid patch containing `$&` (for example, a JavaScript replacement expression) is inserted into the critic prompt as the literal `{{PATCH}}` token instead of the original code, so the reviewer can analyze altered or missing patch content. The bundle and findings insertions at lines 25 and 32 have the same defect.

findings.title: Preserve literal `$` data in prompt substitutions
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing dynamic JSON and patch text as String.replace replacement strings causes `$&`, `$'`, and `$` sequences in that data to be interpreted as replacement patterns. This can alter or duplicate prompt content before it is sent to Codex, causing missed findings.

findings.title: Keep fallback reviews pinned to the analyzed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails, this fallback now omits commit_id. GitHub therefore attaches the review to the PR's latest commit, while the result was computed from headSha. If another commit is pushed during the run, the review body can be reported against code that was never analyzed.

findings.title: Preserve the analyzed commit in the fallback review
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails, the fallback no longer sends headSha. GitHub then defaults the review to the PR's latest commit, so if the PR advances during analysis—or the analyzed SHA differs from the latest—the submitted verdict and findings are associated with a commit the agent did not review. GitHub documents this default behavior: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating records
findings.whyItBreaks: Inputs with invalid severity/category or missing required fields now return a Finding with fallback values such as P1, bug, empty strings, and line 0 instead of throwing. normalizeReview maps these values directly, so malformed review output is accepted as a real finding.

findings.title: Preserve normalizeReview's optional strict parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function previously accepted normalizeReview(raw, strict), including strict=false. Removing that optional parameter is source-incompatible for TypeScript callers that pass the second argument and removes the documented lenient-mode contract.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeFinding no longer rejects invalid severity, category, file, or line values. normalizeReview maps these objects at line 131, so malformed input such as a finding with no fields becomes a returned Finding with severity P1, category bug, empty file, and line 0; callers cannot distinguish this from a real finding.

findings.title: Preserve the normalizeReview strict parameter for compatibility
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported TypeScript function previously accepted normalizeReview(raw, strict), including the documented-by-implementation strict=false path that filtered malformed findings. Removing the parameter is a source-compatible API break for callers passing a second argument, and the permissive behavior is no longer available.

findings.title: Preserve validation errors in normalizeFinding
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeFinding({}) now returns a P1/bug finding with an empty file, lineStart 0, and empty explanation/fix. normalizeReview maps these values into its result instead of rejecting malformed review output, so callers can no longer distinguish an invalid finding from a real one.

findings.title: Keep the explicit repository for pre-checkout PR lookups
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is unset, so these commands run before actions/checkout. Without -R, gh pr view requires a Git repository or GH_REPO context; a clean self-hosted workspace has neither, causing ref resolution to fail. A stale workspace could also resolve the PR against the wrong repository.

findings.title: Keep an explicit repository for manual PR resolution
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch leaves EVENT_HEAD empty, so these commands run before actions/checkout. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh pr view must infer a repository from the current local checkout; a clean runner has none, so the step fails and the review never starts.

findings.title: Preserve explicit repository for manual PR lookup
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty, so these commands run before actions/checkout. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh must infer a repository from the current directory, which is not guaranteed to contain a git checkout on a clean self-hosted runner. Resolve PR refs then fails; a reused workspace may instead resolve a stale or wrong repository.

findings.title: Keep candidate review parsing strict
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing false enables normalizeReview's lenient path, which catches malformed-finding errors and filters those findings. The candidate sent to the critic can therefore omit a real P1/P2 issue, allowing the review to proceed as if no finding existed.

findings.title: Do not drop malformed candidate findings before critic review
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing false enables normalization to discard findings that fail validation instead of propagating the error. The candidate sent to the critic at line 35 can therefore omit a real finding; because the critic is prune-only, the omitted issue cannot be recovered and the final review may incorrectly pass.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review errors instead of returning defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, missing or incorrectly typed review fields threw an error. The new path converts the same malformed input into an apparently valid RawReview with empty/default fields, so callers can no longer distinguish failed review generation from a legitimate empty review and may treat failure as a real result.

findings.title: Preserve rejection of malformed review payloads
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview now converts null, non-object, or missing required fields into an empty/default RawReview instead of throwing. Callers can no longer distinguish malformed review output from a valid review with no findings or checks, potentially treating invalid model output as an acceptable review.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review errors instead of returning an empty review
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation threw when the input or required fields were malformed. The new branches return a RawReview with empty/default fields, so callers cannot distinguish parse/validation failure from a legitimate review with no findings or checks and may accept or report the fallback as real.

findings.title: Resolve the selected PR refs for workflow_dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no pull_request payload, so the checkout ref falls back to github.ref (the branch used to dispatch the workflow), not the PR number supplied by the user. The same path defaults the base branch to main and leaves PR_BASE_SHA/PR_HEAD_SHA empty at lines 45-46. A manual review therefore checks and diffs the wrong commit, or cannot determine the requested PR range.

findings.title: Resolve PR refs before handling workflow_dispatch reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no github.event.pull_request context. The checkout therefore falls back to github.ref, while BASE_REF defaults to main; the requested PR's head and base are not used. Lines 45-46 likewise pass empty PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA. A manual review can consequently analyze the dispatch branch instead of the PR named by pr_number, especially for PRs targeting a non-main branch.

findings.title: Preserve PR refs when manually dispatching the review
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no github.event.pull_request object. The checkout therefore falls back to github.ref rather than the requested PR head, while PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA expand to empty strings. A manual review can inspect the wrong revision or fail to compute the requested PR diff.

findings.title: Preserve the large buffer for git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores spawnSync's 1 MiB default. When the git diff exceeds that size, spawnSync returns ENOBUFS with status null; the helper throws before runLocal can construct the review bundle at line 100.

findings.title: Preserve the large git output buffer
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer makes spawnSync use its default 1 MiB limit. The git diff call at src/adapters/local.ts:100 can exceed that limit, yielding ENOBUFS with status null; the helper then throws and the local review cannot run.

findings.title: Preserve the large buffer for git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores spawnSync's roughly 1 MiB default. For a repository whose git diff exceeds that size, spawnSync returns ENOBUFS with status null, so line 13 throws and runLocal cannot review the change. The previous 64 MiB limit supported substantially larger diffs.

findings.title: Keep review errors as a failing check
findings.whyItBreaks: A review exception is now posted with conclusion "neutral" instead of "failure". GitHub treats neutral required checks as passing, so a failed review can satisfy branch protection and allow the PR to merge despite the message saying it did not pass.

findings.title: Pin the PR diff lookup to the requested repository
findings.whyItBreaks: ghText runs `gh pr diff` without `--repo` and without the supplied cwd. If runGithub is invoked for a checkout while the process cwd is another repository (or not a repository), gh selects the wrong repository or fails, so the review analyzes the wrong patch or aborts.

findings.title: Keep review failures as failing check conclusions
findings.whyItBreaks: When review or posting fails, the check is now submitted as neutral instead of failure. GitHub consumers and automation can no longer distinguish an errored review from a non-failing neutral result.

findings.title: Run gh pr diff against the supplied repository
findings.whyItBreaks: ghText invokes gh pr diff without a cwd or --repo argument, even though runGithub accepts an explicit cwd. If the process runs outside that repository, gh fails or resolves a different repository, so the review cannot obtain the intended PR patch.

findings.title: Keep review-exception checks failing
findings.whyItBreaks: When review(bundle) throws, the check-run conclusion is now "neutral" instead of "failure". GitHub can treat the check as non-failing even though the process exits with code 1, allowing a failed review to bypass the intended merge gate.

findings.title: Keep the reviewer implementation in a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow checks out the PR head and then executes its src/cli.ts while GH_TOKEN has pull-request and checks write permissions. A PR can modify the reviewer to forge results, exfiltrate the token, or execute arbitrary code on the self-hosted runner.

findings.title: Do not install the reviewer from a repository without its package
findings.whyItBreaks: The checked-out repository at this commit contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts. Running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at the repository root therefore fails before the review command can run.

findings.title: Run the reviewer only from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR controls src/cli.ts and the package dependencies installed at line 51, yet this step executes them with a write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN on a self-hosted runner. A malicious same-repository PR can forge review results, exfiltrate the token, or execute arbitrary runner commands.

findings.title: Provide the tool files before installing and executing them
findings.whyItBreaks: This repository's checked-out PR head contains no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts. Therefore pnpm install fails in the workspace, and the subsequent src/cli.ts invocation cannot run. The previous workflow obtained these files from the trusted needlefish checkout.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The command now executes src/cli.ts from the PR head checkout. A same-repository PR can modify that file or install hooks and run arbitrary code on the self-hosted runner with GH_TOKEN, which has pull-request and checks write permissions, allowing forged reviews or runner compromise.

findings.title: Keep the reviewer package and source available at the workspace root
findings.whyItBreaks: This repository's checked-out tree contains no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts. Installing at the PR root therefore cannot install the reviewer, and the next step cannot resolve ./node_modules/.bin/tsx or src/cli.ts, so every review job fails before producing a review.

findings.title: Preserve case and whitespace normalization for severity
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview passes runtime JSON findings through this function. A severity such as " p0 " or "p1" no longer gets canonicalized and is instead classified as P3, silently downgrading the finding's priority.

findings.title: Keep normalizing case and whitespace in severities
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeFinding previously converted values such as " p2 " or "p2" to P2. The new exact-membership check rejects them and returns P3, silently downgrading the finding when normalizeReview processes untyped external input.

findings.title: Preserve case and whitespace normalization for severities
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview passes runtime review data into normalizeFinding at src/shared/schema.ts:132. A raw severity such as " p1 " or "p1" was previously trimmed and uppercased to P1, but now fails the exact membership check and is silently downgraded to P3, changing the reported finding severity.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the spawned Codex process
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting env from spawnSync causes the child process to inherit process.env, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. Codex commands running against a reviewed repository can read those credentials and expose or use them, whereas the previous code explicitly removed them.

findings.title: Prevent GitHub tokens from reaching the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the explicit env object makes spawnSync inherit process.env, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. The Codex subprocess can inspect its environment while processing untrusted repository prompts and return those credentials in its output.

findings.title: Keep GitHub tokens out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the explicit env object makes spawnSync inherit process.env by default, so GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN are available to Codex and any commands it launches. A repository prompt-injection or tool command can read those credentials and expose them through the returned output or other subprocess behavior.

findings.title: Keep fork PRs off the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the same-repository guard causes fork pull requests to run the PR head through pnpm install and src/cli.ts on the self-hosted runner. A malicious fork can modify package lifecycle scripts or the CLI to execute arbitrary code in the runner environment.

findings.title: Keep fork pull requests off the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the repository-origin guard causes fork pull requests to run the checked-out PR head on a self-hosted runner. The workflow installs PR-controlled dependencies and executes PR-controlled src/cli.ts, exposing the runner and its environment to arbitrary untrusted code; it also passes a GITHUB_TOKEN to the review command.

findings.title: Restore the guard that blocks fork PRs on the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: With the job-level repository check removed, any fork can trigger this workflow, check out its own PR head, run pnpm install (including package lifecycle scripts), and execute its own src/cli.ts on the self-hosted runner. That exposes the runner environment and the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN to untrusted PR code.

findings.title: Preserve zero-valued runner grace periods
findings.whyItBreaks: Before this change, an environment value of "0" produced a zero-millisecond grace period. Now it falls back to 5000 ms or 2000 ms, so explicit configuration no longer takes effect: the timeout path at line 124 delays SIGKILL by five seconds, and the give-up path at line 123 is also delayed instead of running immediately.

findings.title: Preserve explicit zero durations for runner shutdown timers
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation accepted finite zero values, so NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 and NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 requested immediate escalation. This change maps those explicit values to the 5000ms and 2000ms fallbacks, delaying hard-kill and give-up handling for processes that ignore SIGTERM.

findings.title: Preserve explicitly configured zero grace periods
findings.whyItBreaks: A value of "0" was previously accepted and caused the SIGTERM grace timer at src/shared/runner-process.ts:124 to fire immediately. It now resolves to the 5000 ms fallback, so configured immediate termination silently becomes a five-second delay; the SIGKILL give-up setting similarly changes to its 2000 ms fallback.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review coverage for unmapped changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: Only the first six mapped hotspots are reviewed. Changed files omitted by the mapper are no longer added to a tail hotspot, so their defects can be silently absent from the final review.

findings.title: Keep a failed hotspot review as a blocking result
findings.whyItBreaks: A runCodex, extractJson, or normalizeReview failure now escapes the hotspot loop and rejects reviewLarge, whereas the previous path returned a review with a blocking residual risk. One transient or malformed deep pass can therefore make the entire large-review workflow unavailable.

findings.title: Forward deep-pass residual risks to the critic
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep pass can report residual_risks, including blocking uncertainty, but the merged candidate now always supplies an empty list. The critic and final verdict lose those failure signals and may approve an incompletely reviewed change.

findings.title: Retain whyItBreaks when deduplicating findings
findings.whyItBreaks: Findings with the same file, line, category, and first 60 title characters but different whyItBreaks text now collide. Only one survives, so distinct effects reported by separate hotspot reviews can be silently dropped.

findings.title: Restore coverage for files outside selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: After truncating to six hotspots, the removed coverage backstop is no longer present. Any changed file omitted by the mapper is never deep-reviewed and no residual risk is recorded, so a large review can report success without inspecting every changed file.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review failures as blocking results
findings.whyItBreaks: A runCodex, JSON extraction, or normalization failure now escapes the loop. Previously it was converted into a blocks=true residual risk; now reviewLarge rejects and returns no ReviewResult at all when any hotspot fails.

findings.title: Forward deep-review residual risks into the critic
findings.whyItBreaks: The deep passes' residual_risks are no longer accumulated; candidateMerged always supplies an empty list. Blocking unresolved evidence is therefore invisible to the critic and can be lost before deriveVerdict evaluates the final result.

findings.title: Include failure rationale in finding deduplication
findings.whyItBreaks: Findings with the same file, line, category, and first 60 title characters now collide even when their whyItBreaks text describes different defects. Only the higher-severity finding survives, silently dropping the other issue.

findings.title: Preserve coverage for files outside the selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews now process only the first six mapped hotspots. Changed files not assigned to those hotspots are never deep-reviewed, so defects in omitted files can produce a false clean review.

findings.title: Do not abort the entire review on one failed deep pass
findings.whyItBreaks: Errors from runCodex, extractJson, or normalizeReview now escape the hotspot loop. One malformed or transient deep-pass response rejects reviewLarge before the critic and verdict are produced, whereas the previous path returned a blocking residual risk.

findings.title: Forward deep-review residual risks to the critic
findings.whyItBreaks: Every successful deep pass can return residual_risks, including blocking uncertainty, but candidateMerged now unconditionally supplies an empty list. The critic therefore cannot distinguish unresolved review gaps from a fully checked large review and may emit PASS.

findings.title: Keep base and head revisions in critic prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review critic now receives only patchStat and candidate findings, not the baseSha/headSha values previously injected. It cannot reliably reconstruct or validate the exact revision range, weakening pruning of findings against the actual diff.

findings.title: Do not deduplicate distinct findings by truncated title alone
findings.whyItBreaks: Findings with the same file, line, category, and first 60 title characters now collide even when whyItBreaks differs. One finding is discarded, potentially hiding an independent defect.

findings.title: Preserve focus propagation for large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: reviewLarge no longer includes bundle.focus in the map prompt and also no longer substitutes {{FOCUS}} in each deep prompt. For a large patch with a non-empty focus, the review agents receive no requested scope and fall back to their default review behavior.

findings.title: Preserve focus when constructing deep-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review path no longer substitutes bundle.focus into deep.md. A non-empty focus value is therefore omitted from every hotspot review, causing focused large-PR reviews to inspect the default scope instead of the caller-requested one.

findings.title: Preserve focus when constructing large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review deep prompt no longer substitutes {{FOCUS}}, and focus is also removed from the map payload. Any caller-provided review focus is therefore absent from both planning and deep-review prompts, so large PR reviews silently review without the requested scope.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into the next minute
findings.whyItBreaks: For durations such as 59500 ms, minutes is 0 while rounded seconds is 60, so renderMarkdown emits "60s" instead of "1m 0s". At 119500 ms it emits "1m 60s". These values are displayed for call and total durations.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For durations such as 59,500ms or 119,500ms, rounding the remainder produces 60 seconds. The renderer therefore emits "60s" or "1m 60s" instead of the canonical "1m 0s" or "2m 0s" in the stats output.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into the minute count
findings.whyItBreaks: The code floors minutes before rounding seconds. For 59500ms it produces `60s`, and for 119500ms it produces `1m 60s`, instead of carrying the rounded second into the next minute.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function is named parsePositiveInteger and its error contract says positive integer, but the changed predicate accepts parsed zero. Consequently "0", "", and whitespace-only strings are returned as 0 instead of rejected, allowing invalid non-positive input through the public parser.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: parsePositiveInteger("0", label) now returns 0, contradicting the exported function's positive-integer contract and its own error message. Public callers can receive a value that the API promises to reject.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported parsePositiveInteger contract promises a positive integer, but the changed predicate accepts 0 and returns it. Callers can now receive a value outside the function's advertised contract.
